claim: The way-and-channel table's row (a) (base l. 2582) lists 'a stage-2 seed's way' among its subjects. Its ladder cell names 'V01 §3.17.3 (3)'s F-TEMPLATE rungs and §4.6's lane ladder', but its test cell is 'T110-2 (3), (5); T-V7-48'. Neither T110-2 clause lays a stage-2 seed: (3) runs S7's intervallum, and (5) runs a quay, an S5b road and an S5c street. The test that runs a stage-2 seed is V01's T-V1-51 (c) (V01 l. 3352), 'every ground crossing of a strip through an `open` span (a `vault` span under a wall read `open`, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*) meeting §4.3's crossing rule', on its named `wallside` fixture. Round-6 note (6) (b) (i) asks each cell to name a test that runs it. The cell names V07's tracker test but not V01's seed test. Nothing built changes.

repair-r6-V04's one HAND-OFF (left open, assemble-r6 §2.1, §9) is unanswered: a locked arch vault in a `vault` span a wall comes to stand over at a regeneration or an epoch. V04 §3.11's UC18 (l. 2459) keeps it ('a reconcile or regeneration that would re-lay, collapse or delete it keeps it — at an epoch reported with E_LOCKED's cause'), as V06 §3.1's protection and §7.2 do; the base's crossing table, *beneath* (l. 2640–2646), says such a span has 'no arch vault in it', whatever the runs' condition, and T-V6-47 bars '0 arch vaults in a `vault` span under a wall'. No trace rule keeps a wall off a locked vault: the pull and cost field avoid only ramps, stairs, feet and an aqueduct's standing supports. So an epoch circuit, contraction or re-anchored stretch, or a ring after New random, laid across the span gives two outcomes: the chamber standing in the band (V04) or removed against its lock (base). At an edit both already refuse (§7.1's lock row; UC18's E_LOCKED).
required_change: Model, §2.7's crossing table *beneath*, after '…so it reads `vault` again, V04 laying its chamber again, once no band or strip lies there.' add: 'A `vault` span whose arch vault is locked or pinned (V04 §3.11's UC18) is held against every wall: a trace laid by the `EnceinteStrategy`'s pull or cost field at a regeneration or an epoch treats its under-deck strip as impassable, as it treats an aqueduct's standing supports; a stretch of the bent group bends locally to cross under the nearest span holding none; a trace that can do neither takes its own ladder (F-WALL at a regeneration, `walls.waited` at an epoch); and by hand a wall over it is refused (`refuse.locked`, §7.1's lock row). So no locked arch vault stands under a wall.' The C8 column description, after 'a lock or pin never refusing work that passes beneath (§7.1's lock row)', adds '— the raised way's lock; a locked arch vault holds its span against a wall (*beneath*)'. V04's END: UC18's outcome adds, after 'refused E_LOCKED until it is unlocked': '; no wall comes to stand over a locked arch vault's span — a trace laid at a regeneration or an epoch keeps clear of its under-deck strip or takes its own ladder, and a hand wall over it is refused E_LOCKED (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'; T-V4-80 (i) adds 'on a CITY fixture whose aqueduct's `vault` span holds a locked arch vault, an epoch circuit across the aqueduct crossing under another span, the vault kept and no wall over it, and a hand `drawWall` across that span refused E_LOCKED'. Scope's END: T110-2 (4) adds 'an epoch circuit across a standing aqueduct whose `vault` span's arch vault is locked — the trace crossing under the nearest span holding none, the vault kept'. (If the program rules instead that a wall outranks the vault's lock at an epoch, UC18 and V06 §3.1 name that exception in the same words, checked against item 101 R13.)

claim: §2.7's support step (7) (base l. 2712–2716) runs '(1)–(5) and the span rule … on the extension alone … to the deck's new end on the new ring, against the obstacles standing then'. (3) (l. 2544–2547) says a merged clear span past `maxClearSpanM` 'drops a generated course (`raised_too_long`, which waits as `raised_too_tall` does, V06 §3.19 (5)) and makes a declared one's dry run bend it'. (4) (l. 2552–2554) says the same for a pier past `maxPierM`. Round 6 wrote that the extension 'keeps the deck's course' and 'is no course laid' (C12 l. 2674–2676; (7)'s last sentence; (M2)'s 'excepted: (7)'), and (6) holds the way ('nothing laid later … drops it'). The frame growth lays new ground and water in the band between the old and new margin (S1, §4.11 *The rung at an epoch*). An extension whose course meets there a river wider than `maxClearSpanM` with no support in its water, or a valley deeper than `maxPierM` (aqueduct 35 m, V11 §3.24.2), has no outcome. Read literally, a generated aqueduct is dropped or 'waits'. But the foot batch has already moved its ring-end foot's ground end onto the new ring (§3.2 (9), l. 3778–3788), so a waiting deck leaves the foot's two ends on different rings, against §3.10's stored-references row ('both ends resolve at every stage end'). A declared way has no dry run at an epoch to bend it. Another builder keeps the course and lays the span or pier past its bound, failing T110-2's 'every clear span and pier within its bound'. Two builds, and no bar runs the case: T110-2's frame clause, T-V4-63 and T-V5-14 extend over open ground.
required_change: (7), after 'against the obstacles standing then,' add: '— where the extension's course meets (3)'s clear-span bound or (4)'s pier bound (a water face or a valley the grown ring reveals), the way, being held ((6)), is neither dropped nor left waiting: the extension's course is bent, as item 101 R2 bends a declared course, to the nearest course from that station to the new ring whose piers and clear spans fit, kept across a band (C12), the ring-end foot's two ends re-placed where that course meets the new rings (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`); with none, it is laid on its course with each span or pier past its bound reported (V06 §2.10's `raised` section) —'. END under scope: T110-2's frame clause adds 'and, on a variant whose grown ring holds, across the aqueduct's course, a river wider than `raisedWays.structure.maxClearSpanM` and, on a second run, a valley deeper than its `maxPierM` — the extension bent to the nearest course whose clear spans and piers fit, the aqueduct kept, nothing waiting, both ends of its ring-end foot on the new rings'. END under V06: §2.10's `raised` section adds `extendedPastBound: number /* frame-growth extensions laid past a support-step bound with no fitting course (§2.7's support step (7)) */`. (If the adjudicator rules the other form instead — the bounds do not apply to an extension, which is no course laid — (7) says so in those words, and T110-2's bound bar reads 'on every course laid'.)

claim: A gate's grip slid into a raised way's under-deck strip has two outcomes. V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` (l. 2103) gives a gate form 'for a gate dropped or slid inside the under-deck strip (T3's **Gate**, a gate's grip)': 'No gate can stand beneath {way}, so it moves {m} m along {wall}.' So a slid gate goes back along the wall and the trace is unchanged. A gate's grip is `moveVertex` on the gate's crossing vertex, 'the crossing way follows' (V09 l. 1194, l. 1703; §7.1 l. 10733: '`moveVertex` on an enceinte's trace — … a gate's crossing among them'). That makes it 'a moved trace vertex', which is row W2 of §2.7's crossing table. W2·C2 reads 'through a gate moved clear of the strip', and its last column says 'a gate it makes for a ground way inside the under-deck strip moved along that way clear of it, the stretch bent locally through it'. §7.1's row (l. 10674) says the same. So in the base the gate moves along its way and the trace bends off its line round the deck strip to pass through it. Only W13 (a `placeGate`) moves a gate along the trace. *beneath*'s gate clause (l. 2646–2652) offers both forms, the second 'where the way is laid after the gate and follows it'. No cell names the slid gate, and no test runs it: T110-2 (4) (l. 18581) and T-V9-52 run only a dropped gate. A builder of the base bends the wall; a builder of V09's line expects it to stay on its line. That is two units with two outcomes for one case, and an untested edge.
required_change: Model (§2.7's crossing table), with ENDs at determinism, scope and V09. (1) §2.7's row W13: '**W13** a hand `placeGate` (§7.1's sugar: a stub crossing the trace at `at`)' → '**W13** a hand `placeGate` (§7.1's sugar: a stub crossing the trace at `at`), or a gate's crossing vertex slid along the trace by `moveVertex` (V09's gate grip)'. Its C2 cell: 'at an `at` inside the under-deck strip, bent along the trace to the nearest point clear of it, the stub with it' → 'at an `at` or a slid point inside the under-deck strip, bent along the trace to the nearest point clear of it, the stub or the crossing way following it, the trace unchanged'. Row W2's event cell: 'a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex or a re-anchored stretch' adds '(a gate's slid crossing vertex is W13)'. (2) END at determinism §7.1's row (l. 10674): 'or a `placeGate` inside its under-deck strip' → 'or a `placeGate` or a gate's slid crossing vertex (`moveVertex`) inside its under-deck strip'. Also 'a `placeGate` moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip' → 'a `placeGate` or a slid gate moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip, its way following'. (3) END at scope's T110-2 (4): after 'a hand `placeGate` inside a viaduct's under-deck strip — moved along the trace clear of it, `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`;' add 'a gate's grip slid along the trace into that strip — moved back along the trace clear of it, its way following, the trace unchanged, `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s gate form;'. (4) END at V09's T-V9-52: after 'a gate dropped on that wall inside the viaduct's under-deck strip moves along the trace clear of it, with `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s gate form' add ', and a gate's grip slid into that strip moves back along the trace clear of it, the trace unchanged, with the same line'.

claim: *beneath*'s *Where the line crosses* (base l. 2617–2635) says "a trace's line never crosses … an aqueduct's standing support", and a stretch laid by no pull or cost field (a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex, a re-anchored stretch, VS3's palisade, V06 §3.7.6 (3)'s quay wall, `repairWall`'s new stretch) "is bent locally, between its nearest points clear of the raised way's under-deck strip … on either side: to cross an aqueduct under the nearest span". That bend is written only for a stretch that crosses the deck line. A hand wall drawn along beneath an aqueduct (between or through its piers), a stretch entering and leaving the under-deck strip on one side, or a stretch drawn or a vertex moved to end at a pier has no "either side" and no crossing to move, so no outcome. Builders differ: move it to the strip's edge, force a crossing under a span (crossing twice), refuse it, or run it through the piers against T-V6-47's bar "0 trace lines across … an aqueduct's standing support". Not in the canon's catalogue; the probe and adjudication-r6 never consider it (pulled and cost-field traces, and road decks, are defined). Distinct from VEW-r6-03 (a barrier anchor or weld vertex inside a strip): no anchor rule reaches a hand stretch run along beneath an aqueduct or ended at one of its piers.
required_change: 1. §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, *Where the line crosses*: after "…through a gate there (by hand a fate named in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line)." add: "A stretch of that group whose line meets an aqueduct's standing support without crossing its deck line there — one drawn along beneath it, one entering and leaving its under-deck strip on one side, one ending at a support — is bent the same way: its part inside the strip moved to the strip's edge on the side it entered from, between its nearest points clear of the strip, an end inside the strip moved to that edge (by hand a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line); so no such stretch runs along within, or ends inside, an aqueduct's under-deck strip." 2. END (determinism), §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row, outcome: after "under an aqueduct's nearest span," add "a stretch along beneath an aqueduct or ending at one of its supports moved to the under-deck strip's edge,". 3. END (scope), T110-2 (4): after "each a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line;" add "a hand `drawWall` drawn along beneath a standing aqueduct through two of its supports, and one ending at a support — each moved to the under-deck strip's edge, a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line, every station, key and span unchanged;". (The adjudicator may instead refuse such a drawing with its nearest lawful alternative under §7.1's catch-all; the bar in 3 then asserts that refusal.)

claim: A held arch vault in a `vault` span that a wall comes to stand over at an epoch or a regeneration (C-wall-raised x C-raised-lock x V04). V04 §3.11 UC18 (V04 l. 2459) says a locked vault element is held 'against every generator: ... a reconcile or regeneration that would re-lay, collapse or delete it keeps it — at an epoch reported with E_LOCKED's cause'. Round 6 made the reconcile delete 'every arch vault ... over which a wall now stands' (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (3), l. 1713). §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, reads such a span `open` with 'no arch vault in it' (base l. 2640-2645). T-V6-47's bar is '0 arch vaults in a `vault` span under a wall' (V06 l. 4170). Nothing keeps a generated trace off such a span. V06 §3.7.1's footprint-distance rule is excepted inside an under-deck strip (V06 l. 1463-1466), and the pull and the cost field bar only supports, ramps, stairs and feet (l. 2622-2625). So an epoch circuit, a contraction or a regeneration's ring (W3) across an aqueduct whose `vault` span holds a locked arch vault has two outcomes: UC18 keeps the chamber in the band; *beneath* and the bar remove it. The same holds for a chamber seating a declared placement (V04 l. 1720-1724), whose building is held (item 101 R13; §7.2, l. 10810). There the band and setback cover its footprint, against §5.3's 'footprints ∩ (wall band ⊕ setback) = ∅' (l. 9290), and *beneath* removes its chamber. repair-r6-V04 filed this as its one open hand-off, 'left open for a ruling; nothing written for it' (assemble-r6 §2.1). No ruling closes it.
required_change: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, at *A `vault` span under the wall*, after '...once no band or strip lies there.' add: 'A wall laid after never comes to stand over a `vault` span whose arch vault is held — locked (V04 §3.11 UC18) or seating a declared placement (V04 §3.5.4 (d)). A trace laid by the `EnceinteStrategy`'s pull or cost field (an epoch's circuit and contraction, a regeneration's ring) treats that span's under-deck strip, widened on each side by the wall strips' widths its rows give (§4.8), as impassable. A stretch laid by neither at an epoch is bent locally to cross under the nearest other span. By hand, the wall's dry run returns E_LOCKED for a locked vault (UC18), and for a declared placement the stretch is bent the same way, a fate. So the vault keeps its chamber, and no footprint enters a band or strip.' Ends: (1) V04: UC18, after 'keeps it', add '— no wall laid after coming to stand over it (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'; T-V4-80 (i) adds the epoch-circuit case. (2) V06: §3.7.1's 'a standing raised way's under-deck strip, supports, ramps, stairs and feet excepted where the trace meets it' adds '(never a `vault` span whose arch vault is held, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. (3) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (4) adds 'an epoch circuit across a standing aqueduct one of whose `vault` spans holds a locked arch vault, and a second run with a declared placement seated in it: the circuit crossing under another span, the vault, its door and the declared building unchanged, 0 arch vaults in a `vault` span under a wall, 0 footprints in a band or setback; and a hand `drawWall` over the locked one returning E_LOCKED'. The adjudicator may instead rule repair-r6-V04's option (a), where the lock yields at an epoch, reported with E_LOCKED's cause; that option still needs the declared-placement case ruled.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x barrier closure, item 106): a barrier anchor or a weld vertex inside a raised way's under-deck strip. *beneath* moves every tower out of the strip: '*No gate and no tower in the under-deck strip* — one the wall's law would place there moves to the nearest point clear of it: a tower along the trace (S7's towers beside a trace an aqueduct at S6's end crossed among them, *over the band*)' (base l. 2645-2648). The barrier closure puts a tower at each anchor: §4.4 S5a (1) 'with a tower at each anchor (§4.8)' (l. 5930, item 106 (a)'s words); §4.8 Towers 'at every barrier anchor (item 106 (a))' (l. 7744); `Enceinte.anchors` 'a tower at each (§4.8)' (l. 2255); PreviewResult.anchors 'each anchor tower's point' (l. 16381); T-V6-47's bar 'its stretches end on tower anchors' (V06 l. 4170). An anchor is the stretch's end, so a tower moved along the trace leaves it bare. *over the band* keeps an aqueduct's strip clear only of 'the trace's gates and towers' (l. 2600). At generation an aqueduct at S6's end is solved before S7 lays any tower, and only 'a tower its spacing would place in the strip' is moved (l. 2601-2603). The case is common where one feature is both the closing barrier and the viaduct's reason: a spur town's gorge side closed by the barrier, with an S4 viaduct across that gorge whose under-deck strip covers the rim where stage 1's trace, laid later at S5a, anchors. Builders differ: one moves the anchor's tower inward (against item 106 (a)'s words and the bars), one keeps it under the deck, one re-anchors the stretch.
required_change: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, after 'a tower along the trace' add: '— never a barrier anchor's or a weld vertex's (item 106 (a), (f); §4.8 *Towers*). A trace laid after a raised way takes no anchor or weld vertex inside its under-deck strip: the `EnceinteStrategy` anchors the stretch at the nearest point of its barrier edge (or enceinte) clear of the strip, and a stretch laid by neither is bent locally there (by hand a fate in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line), so every anchor keeps its tower —'. *over the band*: 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers' -> 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers, and at generation, before S7 lays them, of its barrier anchors and weld vertices'. Second end, at scope: §13.2 T110-2 (3) adds 'a gorge-side CITY whose S4 viaduct crosses the gorge at the rim where stage 1's open stretch anchors — the stretch anchored on the rim clear of the under-deck strip, its anchor tower standing; and (1)'s aqueduct laid at S6's end with its course near a ring anchor — its strip clear of the anchor'.

claim: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath* (l. 2645-2653), bars every gate and tower from an under-deck strip and moves 'one the wall's law would place there ... a tower along the trace ...; a gate along its way, the trace passing through it there ... or along the trace where the way is laid after the gate and follows it'. Two places the wall's law fixes fit neither clause. (1) A river's water gate: the trace 'never crosses water except at a water gate where a river passes', its bank vertices named by `Gate.banks` (§4.4 S5a, l. 5963-5967). It has no way to move along (`way` null), and moving it along the trace leaves the river crossed ungated. (2) The tower at an anchor: g item 106 (a) puts 'a tower at each anchor' (§4.8 *Towers*; `Enceinte.anchors`), and smoothing never moves an anchor (§4.4 S5a (3)); moving the tower along the trace leaves the anchor bare. Both are reachable on a normal CITY site: a stage-2 ring laid after an S4 viaduct that spans a river can cross that river, or end on its bank, inside the viaduct's under-deck strip, because the pull treats only ramps, stairs, feet and an aqueduct's supports as impassable (*beneath*; §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2)). The same holds for an aqueduct at S6's end crossing S3's trace near an anchor: *over the band* keeps its strip clear of 'the trace's gates and towers', but S7 lays the towers later and moves only 'a tower its spacing would place in the strip'. One builder leaves the water gate and gatehouse under the deck (against 'no gate ... in the under-deck strip' and W6's premise); another bends the trace. At an anchor, one moves the tower off it (against item 106 (a)); another moves the anchor. §4.8's lead narrows the rule further: '(one the spacing or the gate law would place there moved clear of it)'. No bar runs either case.
required_change: §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*, *No gate and no tower in the under-deck strip*: after '... (a village track, V07 §3.5a (4))' add '; a gate or tower whose place the trace fixes — a river's water gate (where the trace crosses the river, `Gate.banks`) and the tower at a stretch's anchor (`Enceinte.anchors`; item 106 (a): a tower at each anchor) — moves with the trace: the trace's crossing of the river, or its anchor on the barrier, is moved along the river or the barrier to the nearest point clear of the strip — a trace laid by the pull or cost field treating the river's water and the barrier's edge inside an under-deck strip as no crossing or anchor site, a stretch laid by neither bent locally there (by hand a fate named in `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line)'. *Over the band*: 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates and towers' -> 'its under-deck strip keeps clear of the trace's gates, towers and anchors'. Pipeline end, §4.8's lead: '(one the spacing or the gate law would place there moved clear of it)' -> '(one the wall's law would place there moved clear of it, a water gate's river crossing or an anchor with it; §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. Scope end, T110-2 (3) adds 'and a stage-2 ring whose boundary crosses the river under an S4 viaduct's span and, on a second run, is anchored on that river's bank inside its under-deck strip — the river crossing with its water gate, and the anchor with its tower, moved along the river clear of the strip, the trace laid to them, 0 gates or towers in the under-deck strip'. (The adjudicator may rule another outcome — for example, a water gate lawful under a span whose soffit clears its gatehouse, capped like the run — provided each case has one outcome, item 106 (a)'s tower at each anchor holds and a bar runs it.)

claim: §2.7's crossing table, W11·C2 (l. 2708), reads '*unchanged meeting*: the run (its band, towers, gates) removed, the raised way untouched; V04 lays again an arch vault the run stood over · T110-2 (4)'. T110-2 (4)'s delete case ('a hand `delete` of a run beneath a standing viaduct — the viaduct unchanged, no bend, the run back on its undo', l. 18574-18575) holds no `vault` span. The vault's re-lay on a delete is run by T-V4-63 ('the hand wall's delete laying it again with the same id'), which the cell does not name.

§2.7's support step (3) bounds a slid station by 'both neighbouring spans stay ≤ `raisedWays.structure.slideMaxFactor` × the band's upper bound' (l. 2541). Round 6's (M1) made the obstacle list just before it read 'an enceinte's band (`Enceinte.band`, or before S10 has built it the band beside the standing trace, its half-widths ...)' (l. 2537-2539). So the nearest 'band' is now the wall's band, which has half-widths and no upper bound. The bound meant is (1)'s `pierSpacingM` band (l. 2532), as V11 §2.8c's `slideMaxFactor` comment says ('× the `pierSpacingM` band's upper bound', V11 l. 717).
required_change: §2.7's support step (3): '× the band's upper bound' -> '× the `pierSpacingM` band's upper bound ((1))'.

claim: §2.7's crossing table, row W8's C2 cell (base l. 2705) re-lays an arch vault after `absorbWall` 'once the record is dropped'; T-V6-11 (V6-20, l. 4134) says the same. No op drops a cleared enceinte record. V06 §3.7.2 (3) keeps it in the fortification loop 'until every run is `dismantled`' and keeps it after that as what the `enceinte` provider reads (l. 1488–1499). The rule for the vault reads the band and strip, not the record: *beneath* reads a `vault` span `open` 'while that band or strip lies there, whatever the runs' condition', and V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1) lays the chamber 'once none does'. `absorbWall` merges the strips (band + setback + glacis) into the blocks (V06 §2.8, §3.7.2 (3)), so none lies there from its own commit. `EpochScope.raised` (V06 l. 465, W64) admits the raised way only for 'a wall the epoch laid, moved or removed', and never says whether an absorb counts. Builders therefore diverge: re-lay the vault at `absorbWall`, at the last run's dismantling, or never. T-V6-11's bar has no event to time it by.
required_change: Model, §2.7's crossing table, row W8, C2 cell: 'V04 lays again an arch vault the wall stood over once the record is dropped' -> 'V04 lays again, in `absorbWall`'s commit, an arch vault the wall stood over (its strips and band merged into the blocks, none lies there any more; V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1))'. END V06: T-V6-11 'V04 laying again the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over once the record is dropped' -> 'V04 laying again, in `absorbWall`'s epoch, the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over (its strips and band merged, none lying there)'; §2.1's `EpochScope.raised` comment and W64 'a wall the epoch laid, moved or removed' -> 'a wall the epoch laid, moved, absorbed (`absorbWall`) or removed'; §2.8's `absorbWall` comment 'its strips re-join the blocks beside them' -> 'its strips, the band with them, re-join the blocks beside them (no band or wall strip lies on the old line after it, §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. END V04: the epoch reconcile bullet (l. 2286) 'a wall the epoch laid, moved or removed' -> 'a wall the epoch laid, moved, absorbed or removed'.

claim: Round 6's V09 §4.9 `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 2103) gives the line a gate form "for a gate dropped or slid inside the under-deck strip (T3's **Gate**, a gate's grip)": "No gate can stand beneath {way}, so it moves {m} m along {wall}." A gate's grip is `moveVertex` on the gate's crossing vertex (V09 §3.5, l. 1194; base §7.1's T3 row, l. 10733: "`moveVertex` on an enceinte's trace — a stretch's anchor vertex and a gate's crossing among them"), so a slide is a moved trace vertex: §2.7's crossing table row W2 ("a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex or a re-anchored stretch", l. 2699), whose last column gives "a gate it makes for a ground way inside the under-deck strip moved along that way clear of it, the stretch bent locally through it", and *beneath*'s gate clause puts "a moved trace vertex" in the bent group (the gate moved along its way, the trace bent through it, l. 2646–2652). Only a `placeGate` (row W13, l. 2710; §7.1's bent row, l. 10674: "a `placeGate` moved along the trace clear of the under-deck strip") moves along the trace. So for a gate slid into the strip the base moves it along its road and bends the wall out to meet it, while V09's line says it moves back along the wall.
